article.title: Aristotle Expands Into Rust
article.summary:
We’re excited to announce Aristotle’s expansion into Rust, one of the fastest-growing programming languages for high-stakes software.
Instead of relying on testing to catch every flaw, developers can now use Aristotle to prove their Rust code works as intended before it ships, providing a new level of certainty to systems where even a single bug can be catastrophic.
With support for Rust, Aristotle can prove that your code has no undefined behavior and does exactly what its spec says, even inside unsafe blocks.
If you’re rewriting C in Rust, it can prove the new code behaves the same as the original.
“Aristotle makes formal verification more accessible to Solana developers, helping teams check critical properties of their programs before launch and keep verifying them with every update.”Aristotle for Rust is available today.

What Is A Dirty Bomb?
A dirty bomb is a conventional explosive device combined with radioactive material.
It differs from a nuclear bomb because a regular explosive is used rather than creating a nuclear chain reaction.
A dirty bomb could impact several city blocks, whereas a nuclear blast would vaporize much of a city.

article.summary:
Iran launched a drone attack against a US military base in Bahrain on Sunday, its second attempt to target the country in three days.
The country's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it targeted the US air defence radar facility at al-Riffa air base in Bahrain using six drones.
Bahrain's military said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed the Iranian air attacks "before they could achieve their objectives".
It comes after Iran fired drones at Bahrain on Friday, its first attack against Gulf countries since September.
